text:
Andrei Svechnikov closed out a 9-2 rout of Chicago with 12.5 seconds left, and as Cory Lavalette of the North State Journal noted, that tied the franchise record for goals in a game since the move to Carolina. Six days later he scored twice more against Seattle in Helsinki. He has 11 goals and 21 points in 21 games, with a four-game point streak (5 goals, 2 assists).

This one looks mostly real. His 11 goals come on 9.8 expected, so the finishing is only a little hot, and he is shooting 17.5% against a usual range near 15%. Carolina has scored 4.3 more goals than its chances deserve with him on, which pads the assists more than the goals.

The puzzle is last season. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play, 94th percentile among forwards in expected goals created, yet worth only 0.4 wins above replacement because his finishing lagged and opponents created a lot against him. So far this year the finishing has caught up.

Our projection has him between 29 and 43 goals, 36 in the middle. What to watch: whether the defensive side holds up as well as the scoring.
